newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says medicines move may mean less choice.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says medicines move may mean less choice.

text.p: The UK's opposition Labour party said abolishing price fixing on over-the-counter (OTC) medicines could mean less choice and fewer places to buy them.

In a statement, Labour's health spokesman Kevin Barron said, "it is clear that ending Resale Price Maintenance (RPM) could mean less choice of medicines and fewer places to buy them or to get expert advice."
The UK's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) said earlier on Friday that it would seek to ban RPM on non-prescription drugs.
Labour's Barron said competitive pricing which could result from abolishing RPM might encourage consumers to buy or consume "unnecessary or excessive amounts without referral to a doctor."

RPM allows pharmaceutical wholesalers to put minimum prices on products and supporters claim its abolition would put one in four local pharmacies out of business as larger stores and supermarkets undercut prices.
Barron said if abolishing RPM on OTC medicines threatened small pharmacies, "that would not be in the public interest."
